title: Crypto, Tokenisation and Digital Resilience

maps.tested: Reading 106 rated Very Important; 105 and 107 rated Important. None appears in any exam recall in this dataset, but the recalls predate the current Current Issues cycle, which is replaced annually.
maps.specifics: Because Current Issues rotates every year, the absence of recall evidence carries almost no information. Treat the provider ratings as the only signal available and cover all eight readings: they are 8 questions of the 80.

vardeezReading: CI-6: Important; "Solve book-wise Current Issues questions; anything can show up." CI-7: Very Important; the same note. CI-8: Important; the same note.

selectors.name: Crypto assets and their regulation (CI-6)
selectors.what: Crypto asset definition and the six categories (unbacked crypto assets, NFTs, security tokens, utility tokens, stablecoins, CBDCs); risks and regulatory responses for issuers, exchanges, wallets, validators and banks; national approaches and why a blanket ban is judged ineffective; the BCBS treatment (lower-risk assets with risk weights similar to the underlying, higher-risk unbacked assets with a proposed 1,250% risk weight); the Bali Fintech Agenda considerations.

selectors.name: Tokenisation and market inefficiencies (CI-7)
selectors.what: What tokens and tokenisation are (native versus non-native tokens); trust, sharedness and programmability; frictions across issuance, trading, servicing and redemption and how tokenisation eases them; externalities, internalities and market power; effects on retail investors and brokers; ledger models for sharedness and the conditions under which trust fails (single operator, permissionless, permissioned).

selectors.name: Digital resilience and cyber risk (CI-8)
selectors.what: Cyber risk (loss of confidentiality, integrity, availability from an attack) versus ICT risk (system disruption without an attack); cloud adoption and concentration; how cyber and ICT events become financial and systemic risk (severity lower for confidentiality, higher for integrity and availability; non-linear contagion); macroprudential tools and policy measures (circuit breakers, Sheltered Harbor, SITIs, multicloud, DORA) and the challenges of each.

notSelected: Every learning objective of CI-6, CI-7 and CI-8 is covered by one of the three reading-level shapes; there is no Map specific, August recall or Vardeez pointer beyond them, so no M or V selector is added.
